status: CPU-only prototype; production/default scheduler unchanged; GPU unsupported

mechanism.producer: Wraps the original finalize.padToTargets in one caller-owned operation; records before/after geometry.
validation: Finalized gate-recording source and explicit original witness origins
Canonical zero/one constants and prefix origin/constant/output bounds
Every appended Eq/add/TripleXor/M31ToU32/Blake gate has exact known inputs and consecutive outputs
Exactly four ranges cover every new variable, without gaps/overlap or arbitrary caller-supplied values
Existing Schedule.build independently validates prefix writer/input bounds against prepadding variable count
Range descriptors are revalidated before replay; malformed stored descriptors reject
mechanism.planning: Borrowed prefix Context header/gate slices, no full gate copy. Default Schedule builds only the prefix and allocates its smaller producer/task arrays. Original full padded Circuit remains owned by the caller.
mechanism.replay: One full-size assignment allocation. Existing evaluator replays/checks original prefix gates, then bulk-fills canonical2/0 ranges and checks the FULL padded Circuit.

values.eq: No assigned variables; original0=0 gates retained

mechanism.authority: Generation metadata only. This is not a proof-input format or replacement AIR/PP/receiver authority. No graph hash/cache or per-variable seed list is added.
mechanism.gpu: Plan.requireGpuSupported always returns PaddingRangeGpuUnsupported; no native factory selects this type and no range-init kernel exists.

bounded_fixture.timing_scope: Two test-harness observations on Apple M5 Max. This deliberately padding-heavy fixture is not a representative production prefix or a full-block speedup estimate. Timing includes compact range validation/planning, not padding construction, PP commitment or GPU work.

commands: zig build --build-file src/integrations/riscv_cuda/build.zig check-rv64-ethereum-gpu check-rv64-ethereum-gpu-recursion check-rv64-ethereum-gpu-combined -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu -Dcpu=x86_64_v4+sha -j2
limits: No AIR, PP, constraint, variable shape, public statement or proof wire change.
No claim of fewer AIR cells or fewer kernel launches/depth; padding records can share existing broad waves.
Expected opportunity is less host planning/producer workspace/static generation metadata, not reduced verification work.
No GPU job, budget use, production switch or full proof/basket speedup claim.
Explicit CPU prototype namespace only; main unchanged for review.
